title: Federation Backchannel: Boban Tests the Language
sources: ICTY Prlić et al. Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T), 29 May 2013
Balkan Battlegrounds, Vol. II (CIA, 2002), Federation prelude (pp. 451-455)
content:
By late autumn 1993 the diplomatic ground beneath Herceg-Bosna was shifting. The Owen-Stoltenberg Union of Three Republics had foundered; the ARBiH September-October counter-offensive in central Bosnia had reversed Croat gains around Vareš, Bugojno, and the Lašva valley; and US sanctions pressure on Croatia for its role in the Bosnian war was tightening. Franjo Tuđman, recalculating, signalled to Mate Boban that an overture toward a Croat-Bosniak federation would buy Zagreb diplomatic room it badly needed.

The Prlić judgment records the HZ HB Presidency's federation deliberation as a directed process rather than an organic reconciliation. The Tuđman presidential transcripts admitted at Prlić show Zagreb steering the Herceg-Bosna posture: the federation backchannel was an instrument of Croatian state policy, opened when the costs of the parallel-state project — diplomatic isolation, the indictment exposure of the HVO command, the military reverses — began to exceed its benefits.

Historically the overture matured into the Washington Agreement of March 1994, which ended the Croat-Bosniak war and created the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina on paper. But the autumn-1993 backchannel was the moment before that outcome was fixed: Boban could test federation language, hold to the separate Herceg-Bosna state, hedge with cantonal caveats, or reject the federation path and continue the war against the ARBiH.

The choice recorded here sets whether the Croat-Bosniak war wound down early through a negotiated convergence or ground on toward the externally imposed settlement that history delivered at Washington.
